To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PE5mt-PPE4mt-EspG3mm heterotrimers from the ESX3 system are structurally different from the previously solved heterotrimers of ESX-5.

the structure of the PE–EspG–PPE heterotrimer from ESX-3 reveals how EspG recognizes its cognate PPE substrate, how the C-terminal domain of EspG is dynamic, and that the PPE protein is presented to the chaperones differently by different ESX systems.

we determined the structure of the PE–PE–EspG3 from the ESX system and that this structure reveals that EspG recognizes its cognate substrate through a unique interface that is not present in other EspG–PE–PPE complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of protein secretion in bacteria.
the structure of PE5–PPE3–EspG3, a heterotrimer from Mtb that is involved in the secretion of a set of PE–Ppe proteins.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the secretion of PE and PPE proteins in M. tuberculosis and other pathogenic mycobacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PE–Ppe–EspG interface of the ESX-1 system has a unique complementarity that allows EspG1 to discriminate among non-cognate PE–PEP pairs.
the PPE-EspG interface of each ESX system is unique, and that this unique interface allows each system to discriminate among non-cognate PE–PEP pairs.
the PPE protein is the main determinant of the specificity in the PE–PGE–EspG interaction, with the EspG protein fine-tuning the specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PPE protein from the ESX system is the key to the recognition of cognate PE–Ppe–EspG complex by the secretion machinery, and the EspG from each system has evolved a unique interface to recognize the PPE protein.
each ESX system uses a different mechanism of PE–Ppe substrate recognition by its cognate EspG protein.
the ESX-1–3–5 secretion systems are all distinct and have evolved to secrete a different subset of PE–PEE proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESX-1 and ESX-3 systems have evolved different strategies to interact with their cognate PE–PGE heterodimers.
the PE–Ppe–EspG3 interaction is distinct from other known ESX systems and is likely to be unique for each system.
the PE–Ppe–EspG heterotrimer structure provides a template for understanding the mechanism of substrate recognition in the other ESX systems.
